title: The Lord looketh on the heart (1 Samuel 16:7)
hookLine: the youngest shepherd is chosen, not the tall brothers

lines: A HORN OF OIL, TO BETHLEHEM.
cards: A horn of oil, and a dangerous errand. Samuel is sent to Bethlehem, to the house of Jesse, because God has chosen a king from among his sons. Samuel is afraid: if Saul hears, he'll kill me.
So he goes with a heifer to offer a sacrifice, and invites Jesse and his sons. The first son walks in, Eliab, the eldest, and Samuel thinks: surely this is the one. He looks like a king.
Last time, Israel got a king who stood head and shoulders above everyone. This must be him.

teach.b: And God says no. Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him.
Then the line the chapter turns on: "for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart." Even a prophet, even Samuel, judged by height. Jesse brings the next son, Abinadab.
Not this one. Then Shammah. Not this one.
Jesse makes seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and to each the answer is the same: the LORD has not chosen these. So Samuel asks, almost funnily: are these all your children?

teach.h: THE YOUNGEST, OUT WITH THE SHEEP.
teach.b: Well, says Jesse, there's still the youngest. He's out keeping the sheep. Nobody thought to call him in.
Send and fetch him, Samuel says; we won't sit down until he comes. So everyone waits, standing, for a boy to come in from the field.
And when David arrives, the text describes him: ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look at.

teach.h: HANDSOME TOO, AND THAT'S NOT WHY.
teach.b: The same chapter that says don't look at appearances tells us he was handsome. Some readers find a little joke in that: the point was never that looks are bad, only that they aren't what God goes by.
Arise, anoint him, God says, for this is he.

teach.h: THE LORD LOOKETH ON THE HEART.
teach.b: Samuel anoints him in the middle of his brothers, and the spirit of the LORD comes on David from that day forward. The brothers in the room are passed over; the one left in the field is chosen.

how: Jews read David's anointing in Bethlehem as part of the Former Prophets, and the line that God looks on the heart is studied as a teaching about not judging by appearances.

o: the youngest son, called in from the sheep and chosen
the eldest son, who looked every inch a king
a shepherd hired by Jesse to tend his flocks

games.q: in Jesse's house — tap the pairs.
p: the eldest: surely this is the one
we won't sit down until he comes
poured on David among his brothers

s: Samuel knew from the start that David was the one
he looked at Eliab, the eldest, and thought: surely the LORD's anointed is before him.
the text says David was good-looking
ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look at, in the same chapter that says don't look on appearances.
David was in the room when the sons were presented
he was out keeping the sheep, and they had to send for him.

games.q: you're Samuel. seven of Jesse's sons have passed before you, and God has chosen none of them. what do you do?
o: ask Jesse whether these are all his children.
go home and tell God you couldn't find him.
games.why: Samuel asks: are these all your children? there's still the youngest, out with the sheep. they wait, standing, until David comes in, and he is the one.

practice: Bring to mind someone you've sized up by how they look, sound or dress, or what they do for work: a coworker, a neighbor, maybe you, in the mirror.

Set the outside aside and ask: what do I actually know about their heart, and what have they carried? If you don't know, just notice that; if you pray, hold Samuel's lesson: the LORD looketh on the heart.

wordCard.voice: David. The youngest son left out in the field, ruddy and good to look at, chosen because God looks on the heart, not the height.

orig.note: Hebrew: the heart, what God looks on in 1 Samuel 16:7.

carryVoice: Your line: the heart, not the height. Even Samuel had to learn it. See you tomorrow.
